previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a history of chronic pancreatitis, type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and multiple abdominal surgeries was admitted for acute on chronic abdominal pain. The pain was consistent with a flare of chronic pancreatitis, without evidence of obstruction on CT imaging. He was managed supportively with NPO status, IV fluids, and IV pain control, then advanced to a regular diet as symptoms improved. His blood sugars were low due to poor oral intake, prompting temporary discontinuation of insulin and metformin. Pain and mood improved during the stay. He was discharged home with oral pain medication, Miralax, continued pancreatic enzymes, and instructions to restart diabetes medications when eating normally and blood sugars exceed 130, along with follow-up in outpatient care.

radiology_notes.text:
CHEST RADIOGRAPHS

HISTORY:  Chest pain and cough.

COMPARISONS:  ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Chest, PA and lateral.

FINDINGS:  The heart is normal in size.  The mediastinal and hilar contours
appear within normal limits.  The lungs appear clear.  There are no pleural
effusions or pneumothorax.  Bony structures are unremarkable.

IMPRESSION:  No evidence of acute disease.

CTA OF THE CHEST

HISTORY:  Severe chest and abdominal pain with shortness of breath,
tachycardia and abdominal tenderness.  Prior history of pulmonary emboli, now
off of Coumadin; also history of small bowel obstruction.

COMPARISONS:  A CT of the abdomen is available from ___ and a CT
of the chest is available from ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Following a non-contrast CT of the chest, multidetector CT images
of the chest were obtained with intravenous contrast in the pulmonary arterial
phase.  Sagittal and coronal reformations were also performed.

FINDINGS:  

CT TORSO: Coronary artery calcifications are present.  The heart is normal in
size.  Trace pericardial fluid appears within normal limits.  There are no
pleural effusions.  No enlarged lymph nodes are demonstrated.  There are no
filling defects among the pulmonary arteries.

A small focus of bronchiectasis in the left lower lobe where peripheral
bronchiole is dilated to 2 mm (2:26), which is not significantly changed.  

CT ABDOMEN:  The patient is status post cholecystectomy.  The liver, adrenal
glands and spleen appear within normal limits.  Widespread pancreatic
calcifications are consistent with chronic pancreatitis.  A few small
hypoattenuating foci in the right kidney are too small to characterize but
unchanged.  There is slightly prominent fluid in distal small bowel but
without dilatation or wall thickening.  The post-surgical appearance of the
stomach, small and large bowel is unremarkable, noting prior Puestow surgery
with Roux-en-Y.  There is perhaps a very small umbilical hernia containing
fat, but no substantial ventral hernia.

CT PELVIS:  The prostate, seminal vesicles, and bladder appear within normal
limits.  Patchy vascular calcifications are present.  There is no aneurysm. 
The major mesenteric arteries and veins appear patent.  There is no ascites or
lymphadenopathy.  Small left-sided paraaortic lymph nodes are unchanged and do
not meet CT size criteria for pathological enlargement, although they are
mildly prominent by number but unchanged.

BONE WINDOWS:  Mild-to-moderate degenerative changes are present along the
lower lumbar facets.  There is mild leftward convex curvature centered along
the mid lumbar spine.  There are no suspicious lytic or blastic lesions.

IMPRESSION:

1.  No evidence for pulmonary emboli or other acute process.

2.  Coronary artery calcifications.

3.  No evidence for bowel obstruction.

4.  Findings consistent with chronic pancreatitis, including widespread
pancreatic calcifications, with stable findings status post Puestow with
Roux-en-Y.

INDICATION:  ___ man with right-sided numbness and weakness, to
evaluate for intracranial pathology.

COMPARISON:  CT head without contrast, ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Multidetector CT imaging of the head was performed without
intravenous contrast.

FINDINGS:  There is no evidence of intracranial hemorrhage, edema, masses, or
mass effect.  The gray-white matter differentiation is well preserved.  The
ventricles and sulci are mildly prominent, consistent with mild involutional
changes.  The basal cisterns are normal. Imaged paranasal sinuses and mastoid
air cells are clear.  The orbits are unremarkable.

IMPRESSION:  No acute intracranial pathology.
